rate_source: Banco Central de Cuba official exchange rate for 2022: 24 CUP per USD, fixed by the January 2021 currency unification (Tarea Ordenamiento) and used for official transactions through 2022; from August 2022 a second official rate of 120 CUP per USD applied to retail sales of foreign currency to the public. Confirmed by David's agent on 2026-10-27 from public sources: the Banco Central de Cuba rate table (column TC, USD row) reads 24.00000 in archived captures valid 21-24 Jan, 2-3 Aug, 31 Aug-1 Sep and 8-9 Dec 2022 and 4-5 Jan 2023, and BCC Resolucion 126/2022 (Gaceta Oficial Extraordinaria No. 46, 3 Aug 2022) confirms the fixed single official rate; the 120 rate (column TC Poblacion) applies only to the public and the non-state sector from 4 Aug 2022 (Resolucion 127/2022). The BCC publishes no 2022 average.
decided_by: David (2026-10-27 09:32 UTC: "I'm happy with both of those fixes"; real-terms audit s16/betav5/real_terms_audit/REPORT.md, suggested action 1, at about 24 CUP per USD)
basis: UN AMA values Cuba at 1 CUP = 1 USD (147.1 bn USD in 2022, 62% of XCB GDP) and its peso series (147.1 bn CUP) is not ONEI's post-unification series. ONEI's own 2022 accounts, as reported to UNSD (UN SNA table 1.1, series 300, SNA 1993): GDP 633.44 bn CUP, household consumption 377.85, government consumption 206.08, GFCF 72.71, exports 253.47, imports 309.05. At 24 CUP per USD: GDP 26.39 bn USD; exports 10.6 bn and imports 12.9 bn USD, in line with Cuba's reported trade. At 120 CUP per USD GDP would be 5.28 bn.
